sources.title: Dujiangyan Irrigation System (2026): The Ultimate Guide
sources.content:
Dujiangyan is a 2,200-year-old UNESCO World Heritage Site engineering marvel located approximately 60km northwest of Chengdu. Built in 256 BC by governor Li Bing and his son, the system manages the Min River without using a modern dam, instead employing natural diversion principles inspired by Taoist philosophy.

Quick Facts & Logistics:
Location: Dujiangyan City (60km northwest of Chengdu)
Ticket Price: 80 RMB general admission
Hours: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM (winter closes at 5:30 PM)
Time Required: 3-4 hours for main scenic area
Requirement: Passport mandatory for trains and park entry

Transportation:
High-Speed Train (Recommended): Takes 30-45 minutes from Chengdu
Critical Warning: Book tickets to Lidui Park Station (离堆公园站), NOT Dujiangyan Station
Xibu Station (accessible via Metro Line 2) offers ~10 RMB connections
Tourist buses available from Xinnanmen (~40 RMB, 1.5 hours)
Taxi/Didi options cost 150-200 RMB
Booking Tip: Weekend train tickets sell out rapidly; book 2-3 days ahead.

Historical Significance: Before Dujiangyan's construction, the Min River alternated between catastrophic spring flooding (from Tibetan snowmelt) and devastating dry-season droughts. Li Bing rejected the brute-force dam approach, instead embracing the principle: Channel the water in accordance with its physical properties. This solution simultaneously solved both flooding and drought, transforming the basin into the prosperous Land of Abundance.

How the System Works - Three Components:
1. Yuzui (Fish Mouth Weir): An artificial island in the river's center splits water flow. During dry seasons, 60% diverts toward Chengdu; during floods, the river's physics force 60% of dangerous waters harmlessly down the outer channel.
2. Feishayan (Flying Sand Spillway): A low weir that uses centrifugal force from rushing water to eject silt, boulders, and excess floodwater back into the outer river.
3. Baopingkou (Bottle-Neck Channel): A 20-meter-wide passage carved through Mount Yulei using ancient fire-and-ice cracking methods.

Walking Route (Optimal 3-4 Hour Path):
1. Start at Lidui Park entrance with cedar-lined gardens
2. View Baopingkou's churning water at designated deck
3. Walk to Flying Sand Spillway
4. Cross Anlan Suspension Bridge (historic bamboo rope design, now steel-reinforced)
5. Reach Fish Mouth tip to witness river splitting
6. Climb steep stairs to Erwang Temple (dedicated to Li Bing and son)
7. Summit Qinyan Pavilion for panoramic views
8. Exit via South Gate escalator into Guanxian Ancient City

Nighttime Photography - Blue Tears: The South Bridge features submerged LED lighting that illuminates the Min River's churning white rapids in intense blue.

Dining: Must-Try Specialties: Dujiangyan Baked Potato (crispy pan-fried potatoes with chili and scallions), Hand-pulled Sweet Water Noodles.

sources.title: Dujiangyan Travel Guide - Sichuan Travel Guide
sources.content:
Dujiangyan Irrigation System is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a history of over two thousand years, featuring an ingenious water conservation system that continues to function today.

The Dujiangyan Scenic Area is huge, requiring about 3 to 4 hours to explore. Many visitors arrive around sunset to soak in the vibrant night market town atmosphere.

Key Attractions:
Anlan Suspension Bridge: This picturesque suspension bridge offers a fun and scenic experience and is renowned as one of the top five bridges in ancient China.
Erwang Temple: Dedicated to Li Bing and his son, the masterminds behind the irrigation system, this temple offers breathtaking views of the river.
Guanxian Ancient Town: Located on the left side of the South Bridge, it features stunning traditional architecture.

Best Time to Visit: March to June or September to November. Avoid Chinese New Year (February) and National Holidays (October).

The distance between Chengdu and Dujiangyan is approximately 59 km, which takes about one hour by car. Both Dujiangyan and Qingcheng Mountain are in close proximity, and many travelers combine them into one day trip.

sources.title: Dujiangyan Irrigation System - World's Oldest Waterworks
sources.content:
The Dujiangyan Irrigation System is one of the greatest hydraulic engineering wonders of the ancient world. Built over 2,200 years ago, it is the world's oldest and only surviving no-dam irrigation system.

Stand at the Fish Mouth to watch the river physically split, then climb the steep, winding stairs up Mount Yulei to Erwang Temple, a stunning multi-tiered wooden temple dedicated to Li Bing and his son.

Don't immediately return to Chengdu after touring the park, as Dujiangyan's greatest visual spectacle happens after the sun goes down. The South Bridge near the scenic area's main exit is a gorgeous, multi-tiered traditional Chinese bridge spanning the Inner River.

A general admission ticket costs 80 RMB. Dujiangyan usually takes 2.5-3 hours to explore.

sources.title: 都江堰 - 百度百科
sources.content:
都江堰位于四川省成都市都江堰市城西，坐落在成都平原西部的岷江上，距成都市区约50千米。它是一个庞大的水利工程系统，由渠首枢纽、灌区引水渠道及各类工程建筑物组成，渠首占地面积200余亩。

修建背景：秦昭王后期（约公元前276年至251年），蜀郡守李冰总结了前人治水的经验，组织岷江两岸人民修建都江堰。

主要工程组成：
鱼嘴：位于岷江江心，把岷江分成内外二江。分四六、平潦旱——冬春枯水期内江进水约6成、外江约4成；夏秋洪水期自动颠倒。
飞沙堰：唐代修建的泄洪道，具有泻洪、排沙和调节水量的功能。直径近2米的卵石均能通过飞沙堰排入岷江正流。
宝瓶口：在湔山伸向岷江的长脊上凿开的口子，为内江进水口，起节制闸作用。

主要景点：
二王庙：位于岷江右岸，前临都江堰。原为纪念蜀王的望帝祠，占地约5万余平方米。是古代千年官祭庙，也是二郎神的祖庙。
伏龙观：位于离堆公园内，前殿正中立有东汉时期李冰石像。
安澜索桥：又名夫妻桥，横跨内外两江，被誉为中国古代五大桥梁。全长约500米。
卧铁：埋在内江凤栖窝处的淘滩标志，现有四根分别埋于明万历四年、清同治三年、民国十六年和1994年。

治水经验：
六字诀：深淘滩，低作堰
八字格言：遇弯截角，逢正抽心

所获荣誉：2000年列入《世界遗产名录》。2007年列入全国首批AAAAA级旅游景区。2018年列入世界灌溉工程遗产名录。

旅游信息：成人票80元/人，学生票40元/人。开放时间08:00-18:00。

价值意义：都江堰是当今世界年代久远、唯一留存、以无坝引水为特征的宏大水利工程。建堰2250多年来经久不衰，而且发挥着愈来愈大的效益。担负着四川盆地中西部地区8市41县1165万余亩农田的灌溉。

截至2024年6月3日，都江堰水利工程已经持续运行了2280年零152天。

sources.title: Sichuan Outing Part 3 - DuJiangYan: Pandas and Irrigation
sources.content:
Dujiangyan is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a history of over two thousand years. The scenic area requires about 3 to 4 hours to explore at a comfortable pace.

The highlight is walking across the Anlan Suspension Bridge to reach the Fish Mouth, where you can see the river being split into two channels. The engineering is remarkable for having been built over 2,000 years ago without modern technology.

Erwang Temple offers breathtaking views of the irrigation system from above. The climb is steep but worth it for the panoramic perspective.

Many locals and visitors arrive around sunset to enjoy the evening atmosphere in the nearby ancient town. The night views of the illuminated South Bridge are spectacular.
